text: Mercury is crossing the part of your chart that faces the world, and for a few weeks your mind sits right at the surface. You have more to say than usual, and you say it: opinions arrive faster, questions come easier, and conversations seem to start themselves around you. People meet your thinking before they meet anything else about you right now, which makes this a good stretch for introductions, interviews, pitches, or any moment where you have to speak for yourself. Some of that curiosity turns back on you as its subject. You may catch yourself rethinking how you come across, rewriting the way you describe your work, or noticing your own habits with unusual clarity. Ideas about what you want next tend to surface during these weeks, often mid-sentence, while you are explaining yourself to someone else. That is worth writing down, because self-knowledge produced in conversation evaporates quickly. The cost of a mind this close to the surface is restlessness. Sitting still gets harder, your calendar fills, and you can talk past people without meaning to, since your own thoughts are louder to you than their replies. Listening becomes the skill of the period precisely because it is the one under pressure. If a decision matters, let it rest overnight: the transit favors quick thinking, and quick is not the same as finished. Expect the pace to touch your body a little too, a jumpier attention span, a tendency to fidget, an itch to be somewhere else. Walking while you think helps more than sitting on the impulse. Mercury normally spends two or three weeks in a house, but if it stations retrograde here the visit can stretch toward two months, and the questions about how you present yourself come back for a second and third pass. The reprise is useful rather than annoying. The first pass produces a draft, the return pass produces the edit, and the account of yourself you give at the end of the transit is usually more accurate than the one you started with. When Mercury moves on, the urge to narrate yourself quiets down, and what stays is whatever you said out loud during these weeks that turned out to be true.

For the next little while your mind keeps drifting to money. Mercury moving through your second house puts numbers, price tags, and questions of worth at the center of your attention: what you earn, what you spend, what you own, and whether the arithmetic supports the life you are trying to run. This is not anxiety by itself, though it can turn into that. It is your intelligence doing an inventory. The period suits any task that involves counting or valuing. Reviewing a budget, comparing offers, asking what a service really costs, pricing your own work, or having the pay conversation you have been postponing all go better now, because you can talk about money without the usual fog. Ideas for earning tend to show up too, often small and practical ones: a skill you could charge for, a subscription you could drop, a thing you could sell. Write them down before the transit ends and the mood changes. Conversations during these weeks often circle back to value in the wider sense, what you would give up and what you would not, and it is worth noticing which possessions and commitments you defend when someone questions them. That list is a portrait of you. The risk of the period is loop-thinking. A money question you cannot settle can replay itself at two in the morning without producing a single new fact, and checking the balance a fifth time is not research. When you notice the loop, put the question on paper; a written number holds still in a way an imagined one never does. An ordinary Mercury pass here lasts a few weeks. If a retrograde stretch falls in this house, the stay grows toward two months and financial conversations reopen: the quote gets revised, the invoice needs a correction, the deal wants a second read. Treat the return pass as proofreading rather than bad luck. By the time Mercury leaves, you tend to know your own numbers better than you did, and often you know something subtler as well: which parts of your security live in the account, and which parts were never for sale.

Your days get busy and wordy while Mercury moves through your third house. Messages multiply, small trips stack up, and the week fills with the short-range traffic of ordinary life: errands, calls, forms, quick questions, plans that change twice before lunch. Siblings, neighbors, and the people you see in passing figure more than usual, and a conversation you almost did not have can turn out to be the useful one. Your mind is quick in this period, but wide rather than deep. You pick up facts easily, read faster, learn the new tool in an afternoon, and hold six small threads at once. That makes this a good stretch for correspondence, local logistics, classes that meet weekly, and any writing that comes in short pieces. It is a weaker stretch for the one long task that needs unbroken hours, because the doorbell of your attention keeps ringing. If something deep is due, guard a block of time for it on purpose; the period will not hand you one. Expect a little scatter. Double-booked slots, a missed exit, the email sent to the wrong thread: none of it is fate, all of it is load. Slowing your speech slightly and rereading before you hit send removes most of the damage. A normal pass through this house takes a few weeks. When a retrograde falls here, the visit can run two months or so and the traffic turns repetitive: the plan reschedules, the message needs a clarifying follow-up, the paperwork comes back for a signature you missed. Build slack into the calendar and the reruns stay small. There is real pleasure available in these weeks if you let the pace be what it is. Curiosity is cheap and everywhere: the half-hour detour, the question asked of a stranger, the library book actually read. When Mercury moves on and the noise drops, you tend to find that the scattered little inputs added up to a surprisingly useful picture of your own neighborhood, in every sense of the word.

Mercury has dropped to the base of your chart, and your thinking turns toward home. For a few weeks the conversations that matter happen in the kitchen rather than the conference room: talks with family, decisions about the household, the roommate question, the repair estimate, the call with a parent that goes longer than planned. Practical matters of place tend to need words now. Leases, listings, insurance forms, the folder of house documents nobody opens, all of it benefits from your attention while your mind is pointed this way. If you can work from home during this period, the arrangement suits you, since your best thinking currently wants a familiar chair. Memory gets talkative too. Old photographs, family stories, the way a smell brings back a hallway from childhood: the past supplies more of your mental material than usual, and you may find yourself rewriting scenes from years ago in your head. That is not wasted time. Understanding how your household of origin talked, or refused to talk, explains a good deal about how you handle a difficult subject today, and these weeks make the pattern easier to see. The hazard in these weeks is staleness. Thinking that never leaves the house can start chewing on itself, and a family discussion can slide from useful to circular without anyone noticing the turn. When a conversation starts its third lap, write down the two real options and stop talking for the night. An ordinary visit runs a few weeks; a retrograde here stretches it toward two months and tends to reopen domestic threads, the relative who calls back, the repair that needs a second visit, the moving plan that shifts. Let the revisions happen. Homes are edited over time, not settled in one pass. By the end of the transit you usually know more clearly what you need from the place you live and from the people in it, and you have probably said at least one thing at the table that had waited years to be said. Quiet weeks, on the whole, but not empty ones.

Wit comes back into season for a few weeks. Mercury moving through your fifth house makes words a form of play: banter sharpens, jokes land, flirtation runs on good sentences, and the fun of an evening often turns out to be the conversation itself. If romance is in the picture, or could be, this period favors the talking stage in the best sense, the long messages, the shared jokes that become a private language, the discovery that someone's mind is attractive. Creative work wants words now too. The idea you have been circling becomes a draft, the hobby acquires a notebook, the song gets a lyric. Projects done for pleasure move faster than projects done for duty in this stretch, so give the pleasurable one an hour and watch what happens. Games of skill and strategy also thrive. Your mind wants to play, and it plays to win. If there are children in your life, expect more conversation with them, and better conversation than usual. Kids tend to say the interesting thing during this transit, and explaining something to a child will show you what you actually understand about it. The risk is lightness that refuses weight. Charm can slide into performance, teasing can nick someone without your noticing, and a clever reply can win the exchange while losing the person. If a talk turns serious, let it be serious; the wit will keep. A typical pass lasts a few weeks, though a retrograde can hold Mercury here for a couple of months, in which case old amusements resurface: a former flame writes, an abandoned project asks for another look, a game you quit invites a rematch. Some of those returns deserve the second chance and some are just reruns, and a week of watching usually tells you which. What this period leaves behind, once the sparkle moves on, is often a small finished thing, a piece, a poem, a running joke, proof in your own handwriting that your mind knows how to enjoy itself.

The details start asking for you. With Mercury moving through your sixth house, attention drops from the big picture to the working parts: the schedule, the inbox, the checklist, the system that almost works and the one that quietly does not. For a few weeks you see the loose screws of daily life with uncomfortable clarity, and that same vision makes this one of the better stretches of the year for tightening them. Work absorbs most of the traffic. Processes get documented, handoffs get clarified, the recurring meeting finally gets an agenda. Expect more back-and-forth with the people you share tasks with, and better results when instructions are written down rather than assumed. If you have been meaning to reorganize anything, files, tools, the desk itself, your patience for tedium is unusually high right now, and tedium is where order comes from. The body joins the list too. Routines around sleep, food, and movement become interesting as information: you notice patterns, track things, read up, bring questions to the appointment you finally booked. Treat what you learn as notes to discuss with someone qualified rather than conclusions to act on alone. The trouble this period invites is miniature. A mind tuned for detail can start grading everything, and worry does an excellent impression of diligence. If you have checked a thing three times, the fourth check is anxiety wearing a badge. The cure is a boundary: a list with an end, a workday with an end, an evening where nothing gets optimized. Mercury usually clears a house in a few weeks. A retrograde here can extend the stay toward two months and send the fixes back for revision, the process that needs a second draft, the order that arrives wrong, the appointment that moves. Annoying, but the second version is usually the one that holds. When the transit ends you inherit whatever you tightened. A calendar that tells the truth and a routine that runs without friction are quiet gifts, and these are the weeks when they get built.

For a few weeks the important sentences are the ones spoken across a table. Mercury moving through your seventh house pulls your mind into dialogue with a partner, a close friend, a business associate, a counterpart, anyone who stands on the other side of a we. Thinking alone produces less than usual in this period; thinking out loud with one other person produces more. Use that for the conversations that need two people. The talk a marriage or long partnership has been postponing goes better now, because you can hear the other position as a position rather than as an attack. Negotiations, interviews, and consultations sit under the same weather: terms want to be discussed, agreements want to be put into words, and the contract that has been sitting in a drawer wants a careful read before anything gets signed. Expect the other person to be articulate too. Whoever you deal with in this stretch tends to bring arguments rather than moods, which is bracing when you agree and instructive when you do not. You may notice your own opinions sharpen in response, since a good opposite number shows you the exact edges of what you think. One hazard is losing your voice in the exchange. Agreeableness can shade into echoing, and you can leave a discussion having adopted a view you never actually held. After a strong conversation, take an hour alone and check which conclusions are still yours. The reverse failure exists too: debating to win, scoring the point and souring the room. The period rewards the middle course, stated views and open ears. An ordinary pass here runs a few weeks. If Mercury retrogrades in this house, the stretch approaches two months and dialogues reopen, the agreement that needs a revised clause, the misunderstanding that wants a second and calmer airing. Reopened is not broken; most partnerships are maintained exactly this way. What the transit leaves behind is usually a clearer account of where you and the people closest to you actually stand, spoken rather than assumed, and that alone is worth all the talking.

Your mind wants to go under the surface for a while. Mercury moving through your eighth house turns your attention to what is shared, hidden, or hard to say: joint money, debts and taxes, inheritances and insurance, the private mechanics of intimacy, the subjects that go quiet when they enter a room. For a few weeks you have an unusual stomach for exactly these topics, and that appetite is the point of the period. The paperwork side is real and worth doing. Anything involving money you hold with others, accounts, loans, estates, claims, or settlements, rewards your attention now, because you are willing to read the fine print and ask the blunt question. If a financial arrangement with a partner or an institution has been running on assumptions, these weeks favor putting it into words and onto paper. The emotional side runs deeper. Conversations can reach places they normally avoid: what someone actually fears, what a relationship actually costs, what happened in a family and was never discussed. You may find yourself researching with real intensity, pulling a thread through records or history or psychology until it gives up its knot. Secrets have a way of surfacing under this transit, sometimes yours, sometimes other people's, and discretion becomes a live skill; what you learn in these weeks is not automatically yours to repeat. The snag is fixation. A probing mind can circle one dark spot until the circling feels like depth, and suspicion can dress itself up as insight. If you catch yourself rereading the same message for hidden meaning a fourth time, the meaning is in you, not the message. Mercury typically clears a house in a few weeks, though a retrograde can keep it here toward two months, in which case settlements revise, estimates come back changed, and a buried subject returns for the deeper second conversation it deserved. When the transit ends, the mood lifts on its own. What stays is what you cleaned: an arrangement made explicit, a truth said out loud, a question you finally asked and survived.

The questions get bigger for a few weeks. Mercury crossing your ninth house lifts your attention off the daily grid and points it at the horizon: travel, study, belief, law, publishing, the frameworks that explain why any of the small stuff matters. You think in wholes during this period, and the appetite for meaning is genuine, not decorative. Plans benefit first. Trips get researched, courses get compared, applications get drafted, and the far-off idea acquires an itinerary and a price. If your work touches teaching, writing for an audience, academia, law, or anything international, expect more traffic than usual and better ideas about where it should go. Long-form input suits you now: the serious book, the lecture series, the conversation with someone whose world differs from yours. Perspectives from outside your own culture are worth actively seeking in these weeks, because your mind is unusually willing to be rearranged by them. Your opinions are also under construction, whether you notice or not. Positions you have held by habit get inspected, and some fail the inspection. Letting a belief go can feel like losing ground; it is usually gaining accuracy. The pitfall now is the sermon. A head full of conclusions wants an audience, and enthusiasm for your current view can turn conversations into broadcasts. The test is simple: if you cannot state the opposing case fairly, you have stopped thinking and started preaching, and the people around you noticed before you did. A standard pass through this house lasts a few weeks. A retrograde stretch extends it toward two months and sends the big plans back for revision, the itinerary that changes, the application that wants another draft, the argument you thought settled that reopens with better evidence. Revision at this scale is cheap now and expensive later, so take it. By the end of the transit your map is larger than it was. Not finished, since maps never are, but larger, and a few of the roads on it are ones you drew yourself after actually going to look.

Mercury is moving across the most visible part of your chart, and for a few weeks your words travel farther than usual. What you say at work gets repeated, what you write gets forwarded, and the offhand remark in a meeting can end up quoted in a decision. The period puts your thinking on the record, which is an opportunity and a caution in equal measure. Use the reach deliberately. Presentations, proposals, reports, applications, and conversations with people in authority all sit well in this stretch. You can explain your work clearly right now, and clarity is most of what advancement runs on. If you have been waiting to raise a professional question, ask for the meeting during these weeks. If your role involves speaking for a team or an organization, expect more of that than usual, and prepare a little more than feels necessary, because the audience is larger than the room. Your own direction comes up for review as well. The transit favors thinking concretely about the career itself: where the current path leads, what the next role requires, which skills the plan is missing. Ambition benefits from being written down. A goal stated in a sentence can be tested, while a goal kept as a feeling can only be worried about. The temptation in these weeks is speaking for effect. Visibility tempts polish over substance, and a reputation built on saying things well eventually gets asked to deliver. Promise at the pace you can produce. Mercury's stay here normally runs a few weeks, but a retrograde can stretch it toward two months and put public words through revision: the announcement that moves, the proposal that returns with comments, the title or plan that gets renegotiated. Frustrating in the moment, and usually the better outcome, since work that survives an edit stands longer. When the transit passes, the spotlight on your sentences dims, and what remains is whatever you committed to while people were listening. Choose those commitments as if they will be remembered, because in these weeks they will be.

Your ideas want company for a while. Mercury moving through your eleventh house carries your mind out into the circle: friends, allies, teams, communities, the group chat that is secretly a committee. Conversation multiplies in these weeks, and it is conversation with a direction, less about the day, more about what a number of people could do together. Plans for the future are the natural material. Goals you have carried privately benefit from being said out loud to friends now, because the reactions are unusually useful: one person knows the shortcut, another knows the obstacle, a third knows someone you should meet. Reaching out to the acquaintance you admire tends to get a reply in this period, and the introduction you have been meaning to make finally happens in a sentence. Groups you belong to may need more words than usual, the meeting, the vote, the plan for the year, and you are good at supplying them. Your role in these weeks is often the clarifier, the one who turns a room's vague enthusiasm into a list with names next to tasks. It is quiet work, and it is the difference between a group that talks and a group that does. Friendship itself gets more verbal too. Expect catch-ups, long threads, the conversation that updates a friendship to the current versions of both people. One of those talks may quietly matter more than everything else in the transit. The danger is dispersal. Ten conversations about the plan can replace the plan, and a goal discussed widely enough starts to feel accomplished. If the idea is still just talk after two weeks of talking, give it one owner and one next step, even if both are you. A typical pass runs a few weeks; a retrograde can lengthen the stay toward two months and rerun the social traffic, old friends resurfacing, group decisions reopening, an idea from months ago suddenly viable. When Mercury moves on, you keep the connections you refreshed and, often, a future plan that several people now believe in because you were the one who put it into words.

The volume drops for a few weeks. Mercury drifting through your twelfth house pulls your mind below the waterline, into the private, the unfinished, and the not yet sayable. You may notice you have less to announce and more to consider: conversations tire you sooner, solitude gets productive, and your best thinking happens in the margins, on walks, in the shower, in the notebook nobody reads. Take the hint rather than fighting it. This is a drafting period, not a publishing one. Ideas conceived now often need to stay private a little longer to survive, because shown too early they wilt under other people's opinions. Keeping your own counsel for a stretch is not secrecy, it is incubation, and projects that begin quietly here have a way of surfacing well formed a month or two later. The material that comes up can be old. Memories, regrets, dreams with speaking parts, the conversation from years ago that suddenly replays with new subtitles: your mind is doing end-of-cycle filing, deciding what to keep. Journaling suits the period unusually well, and so does any talk that happens in confidence, with a trusted friend or counselor, anyone safe enough for half-formed sentences. Listening, in general, outperforms speaking now. The risk is fog. Thoughts left entirely unspoken can loop and distort, small worries inflate in the dark, and you can drift through a meeting having heard none of it. Anchor yourself with small concrete acts: write the thought down, name it to one person, finish one visible task a day. A normal pass here lasts a few weeks. If Mercury doubles back, the quiet stretch runs toward two months, and old private threads, the unsent letter, the unresolved apology, the shelved idea, return asking to be completed. Completing even one of them is the real work of the transit. Then Mercury crosses into daylight, the words come back, and you usually find that the quiet weeks wrote more than the loud ones ever do. You were composing the whole time, just not out loud.
